title: [PDF] FY 2026 President's Budget - Commodity Futures Trading Commission
summary: The CFTC submitted its FY 2026 budget request of $410.0 million and 650 FTE, representing a 12.3% increase over FY 2025 enacted levels. The document outlines organizational structure, divisional budgets, and regulatory statistics for derivatives markets including DCMs, DCOs, SEFs, FCMs, and SDRs. This is a government administrative/appropriations document with no market-moving content or policy decisions.
key_points: CFTC requests $410.0 million and 650 FTE for FY 2026, a 12.3% increase above FY 2025 enacted budget
Division of Market Oversight budget section covers Swap Execution Facilities (SEFs) and Designated Contract Markets (DCMs) registration and oversight
Division of Clearing and Risk covers central clearing infrastructure and derivatives clearing organizations (DCOs)
FY 2024 data shows: approximately 15 registered DCMs, multiple DCOs including SIDCOs (Systemically Important DCOs), 14 provisionally registered SEFs
Source includes statistics on swaps volume (cleared vs. uncleared), customer funds in FCM accounts, and margin requirements
Document is from May 2025 for FY 2026 (October 2025–September 2026), making it a historical administrative record as of TODAY
why_it_matters: This budget document provides background context on U.S. derivatives market regulatory infrastructure—registration counts, trading volumes, clearing statistics. It does NOT contain policy changes, market analysis, or macro catalyst information. Archival value is limited to understanding the CFTC's organizational capacity and scope.
market_structure_context: The document provides a snapshot of U.S. derivatives market infrastructure as of FY 2024 data: registered DCMs (contract markets), DCOs (clearing organizations including systemically important SIDCOs), SEFs (swap execution facilities), FCMs (futures commission merchants), and SDRs (swap data repositories). Volume statistics show growth in futures and swaps traded, with cleared vs. uncleared breakdowns. This represents the regulatory landscape for derivatives market structure but does NOT contain policy changes, market analysis, or market-moving signals.
